cards.text: Solomon is king of Israel, and people are TALKING. The queen of Sheba hears about the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the LORD. And friend, she doesn't just nod and move on.

cards.question: The queen of Sheba has heard all about Solomon's fame. Why does she come to see him?

answers.text: To test him with hard questions
To end a war between them

cards.text: She rolls into Jerusalem with a very large caravan, camels loaded DOWN. Me? I came out of a clearance bin with a 25 cent sticker on me.

cards.question: What are the queen of Sheba's camels carrying into Jerusalem?

answers.text: Spices and gold and precious stones
Wool and bronze and fine linen

cards.text: Then she sits down with Solomon and tells him everything that's on her mind. Every hard question she brought, right there on the table.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon runs into a question from the queen of Sheba that's too difficult for him to explain.

cards.text: Then she sees it all: his wisdom, the palace he built, the food at his table, his servants and attendants, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presents at the house of the LORD.

cards.question: After seeing Solomon's wisdom, his palace and his whole court, how does the queen of Sheba react?

answers.text: She finds it a bit much

cards.text: She tells the king, "The report I heard in my own country about your words and wisdom is true." Friend, nobody has EVER traveled that far to say my reviews were true. I came with a price sticker.

cards.question: True or false: The queen of Sheba believed the report about Solomon before she came and saw it with her own eyes.
Now that she's seen it, how much of the real thing does the queen of Sheba say the report told her?

cards.text: Then she says, "How blessed are your men! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!" I think she'd trade places with the STAFF in a heartbeat.

cards.question: Next the queen of Sheba says someone else is blessed too. Who?
The queen of Sheba says that because of the LORD's eternal love for Israel, He made Solomon king to carry out justice and ___.

cards.text: Then she hands the king her gifts: 120 talents of gold, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones.

cards.question: True or false: After the queen of Sheba's gift, spices never again came in to Solomon in such abundance as hers.

cards.text: Quick side note in the text. Hiram king of Tyre (1 Kings 5:1) has a fleet bringing gold from Ophir, and it also hauls in a great cargo of almug wood and precious stones.

cards.question: What does Solomon make out of the almug wood Hiram's fleet brings in?

cards.text: King Solomon gives the queen of Sheba whatever she asks for, plus gifts out of his royal bounty, and she heads home with her servants. WHATEVER she asks. Friend, I asked that junk drawer for a little elbow room once and got a takeout menu in the face.

Now the writer opens the books on Solomon's wealth: 666 talents of gold a year, plus what the merchants and kings bring in. Gold shields, gold drinking cups, ships of Tarshish hauling in gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks, and a great ivory throne overlaid with pure gold, with twelve lions on its six steps. Nothing like it had ever been made for any kingdom. Friend, the Millers got ME for a quarter.

cards.question: True or false: King Solomon surpasses all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
The whole world comes to hear Solomon's wisdom. Where did that wisdom come from?

answers.text: God put it in his heart
The queen of Sheba taught him

cards.text: Year after year, visitors bring tribute: silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses and mules. Solomon gathers 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses and makes silver as common in Jerusalem as stones. His horses come in from Egypt and Kue, and chariots and horses go out again to the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram. Twelve THOUSAND horses, friend, and you thought finding parking downtown was rough.

findings.problem: This fill in the blank asks the baker to guess the next word of the queen's line, 'justice and ___'. The baker hasn't seen the wording and can't reason it out. 'Glory' is also close enough to argue for.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote, 'Friend, nobody has EVER traveled...' and 'I came with a price sticker.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click. 'Nobody traveled that far to say my reviews were true' brings in reviews he never had. Then 'I came with a price sticker' doesn't connect to reviews or to a report being confirmed. A stranger would say huh?

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the two exclamations quoted from 10:8, plus 'I think she'd trade places...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'King Solomon gives...', 'WHATEVER she asks.' and 'Friend, I asked that junk drawer...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This card is a flat list of what the queen sees, with none of Papa Dorin's voice. It reads like a summary, not a storyteller.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This card lists the queen's gifts with no voice or reaction at all. That's flat for a moment as big as 120 talents of gold.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Three of the walkthrough's jokes use the same premise, his cheap 25 cent price: stop 1 card 3 ('25 cent sticker'), stop 1 card 9 ('I came with a price sticker') and stop 2 card 1 ('the Millers got ME for a quarter'). The humor ends up repetitive across the lesson.
findings.question: Should the docs limit how often one joke premise or callback is reused in a single lesson? papa-dorin.md says 'No formula' and 'no joke quotas' but doesn't address repetition.
